verdict: HPIOV2-001 is fixed. HPIOV2-002 is fixed for state preflight, count/byte caps, census, and the tested mid-file TrustedIoError cleanup, but is not closed for two handled/raw fsync failure points immediately around temp publication. One focused local revision remains. This is not a whole-launch verdict; HPIO-003, stable-root-across-restart, actual T16, and other root gates remain open.

finding_disposition.code_evidence: _read_state now compares final_lock.execution_config_sha256, outer_training_manifest_sha256, and hidden_features_manifest_sha256 to final_refit_admission (trusted_io.py:1028-1048).
finding_disposition.behavior_evidence: The exact 27-test suite passed. In three separate restart-check Python processes, each field mutation returned STATE_CORRUPT.

finding_disposition.verified: admit_intent preflights next state before store (338-344); census and explicit max_snapshot_count/max_snapshot_bytes block new stores (557-618); a forced _replace_at research failure after temp identity capture removed the local temp; max_state_bytes=400 left no rejected canonical store; exact count and byte boundaries stopped before extra directory creation; known crash temp evidence counted and remained preserved.
finding_disposition.remaining: See HPIOV3-001. Temp identity is captured only after the first snapshots-directory fsync, and a later explicit completed-temp fsync is outside OSError conversion/TrustedIoError cleanup.

new_findings.title: Two pre-rename fsync failure paths bypass complete handled-temp cleanup
new_findings.code_evidence: After os.mkdir(temp), os.fsync(snapshots_fd) runs at 647-650 before temporary_identity is captured at 651-654. Its OSError is converted to TrustedIoError, but outer cleanup at 671-674 cannot run because identity is None. The explicit os.fsync(temporary_fd) at 660 is outside an OSError wrapper; the outer clause catches only TrustedIoError, so a failure bubbles raw OSError and skips cleanup.
new_findings.behavior_evidence: Injected failure of the first snapshots-directory fsync returned UNSAFE_FILE but left stale_temps=1 and no state. Injected failure of the explicit completed-temp fsync returned raw OSError, left stale_temps=1, and published no state. The already-authored research-file TrustedIoError case did clean entries to zero.
new_findings.impact: The new cap census will preserve/count these remnants on later calls, so safety remains fail closed. However, the stated handled-failure cleanup is incomplete, one public path violates the TrustedIoError/safe-enum discipline, and avoidable capacity can be consumed.
new_findings.required_fix: Open the just-created temp and capture its device/inode before the first parent fsync. Normalize all non-crash OSErrors through a cleanup-capable block: attempt identity-checked cleanup, then raise TrustedIoError(UNSAFE_FILE). Preserve BaseException/process-crash evidence. Add one regression for post-mkdir parent fsync failure and one for the explicit completed-temp fsync failure; assert safe enum, zero temp entries, and no admission.

verified_boundaries.max_state_400: Two candidates fit. The next call returned LIMIT_EXCEEDED and its closure was absent; stored directory count equaled accepted count.
verified_boundaries.snapshot_count: With max_snapshot_count=2, outcomes were ACCEPTED, ACCEPTED, LIMIT_EXCEEDED and directory count remained 2.
verified_boundaries.snapshot_bytes: One snapshot with exact logical size 385 was accepted; limit 384 returned LIMIT_EXCEEDED and created zero directories.
verified_boundaries.crash_incomplete: A known .snapshot-<32hex> partial directory consumed max_snapshot_count=1, blocked the canonical snapshot with LIMIT_EXCEEDED, and remained preserved.
verified_boundaries.production_draft_arithmetic: Five max_closure_bytes=393216 closures plus five canonical 350-byte manifests total 1967830 logical bytes; max_snapshot_bytes=2097152 leaves 129322 bytes headroom. Census also counts known incomplete evidence, so it can only reduce remaining capacity.
verified_boundaries.historical_non_regression: Historical A remained selected/copied after B and final_refit intent; active solution differed.
verified_boundaries.limitations: Logical byte census excludes directory metadata and is not a filesystem quota. It is safe only with the documented stable trusted state-root TCB and root attempt limit.
